QuestionText: What is the action of heat on potash alum?
ExplanationText: The chemical formula of potash alum is KAl(SO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>2</sub>.12H<sub>2</sub>O. On heating its crystals moderately, it loses the water of crystallisation and then liquefy and becomes fluffy. If heating continues, the water is driven off and it gets converted into anhydrous powder of potassium aluminium sulphate [KAl(SO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>2</sub>].

QuestionText: What is the correct ratio of aluminium, potassium and sulphate ions in a formula unit of potash alum?
ExplanationText: The chemical formula of potash alum is K<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>.Al<sub>2</sub>(SO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub>.24H<sub>2</sub>O or KAl(SO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>2</sub>.12H<sub>2</sub>O. Hence, the ratio of aluminium, potassium and sulphate ions in a formula unit of potash alum is 1:1:2.

QuestionText: What is the nature of the substance added during the formation of potash alum to avoid the hydrolysis of Al<sup>3+</sup> ions?
ExplanationText: An acidic substance, dilute H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>, is added during the formation of potash alum to suppress the hydrolysis of Al<sup>3+</sup> ions.

QuestionText: Which of the following mixtures is used to wash the crystals of potash alum formed during the experiment?
ExplanationText: The crystals of potash alum are washed with a cold water-alcohol mixture to remove adhering impurities while minimizing the loss of alum crystals.

QuestionText: Which of the following is true about the aqueous solution of potash alum?
Option2: It has no effect on litmus paper
ExplanationText: Potash alum dissociates in water to produce K<sup>+</sup>, Al<sup>3+</sup> and SO<sub>4</sub><sup>2−</sup> ions. Al<sup>3+</sup> gets attracted towards the lone pair of electrons present on the oxygen in water molecules and thus undergoes hydrolysis. Al<sup>3+</sup> + 6H<sub>2</sub>O ⇌ [Al(H<sub>2</sub>O)<sub>6</sub>]<sup>3+</sup>; [Al(H<sub>2</sub>O)<sub>6</sub>]<sup>3+</sup> + H<sub>2</sub>O ⇌ [Al(H<sub>2</sub>O)<sub>5</sub>(OH)]<sup>2+</sup> + H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup>. It is due to the hydrolysis of Al<sup>3+</sup> ions that H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup> ions are produced, and hence, the aqueous solution of potash alum is acidic. Thus, it can turn blue litmus red.
